extracted.intended_audience: feature/longform journalists, journalism students, and editors interested in New Journalism techniques
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for producing feature/longform journalism in the New Journalism tradition (Tom Wolfe / contemporaries): scene-driven, character-centered reporting using literary techniques while maintaining factual accuracy. Focuses on what makes a subject and reporting approach suitable for this style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scene-by-scene construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell the story through scenes rather than historical narrative summary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct the piece as a sequence of scenes—show actions and interactions as they occur instead of summarizing events in overview. Emphasizes dramatic, present-tense-like rendering of moments to create narrative momentum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialogue in full
rubrics_metrics.description: Conversational speech recorded as it actually happened (not just official quotes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include extended, verbatim exchanges to reveal character, dynamics, and subtext; avoid relying only on brief attributed quotes. Must still obey factual rules (see 'No invented dialogue').

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-person point of view
rubrics_metrics.description: Present every scene through the eyes of a particular character (interior thoughts where possible).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a scene-specific POV so readers experience events via a character's perceptions; where available, incorporate interior thoughts to deepen psychological portrait (Talese/Wolfe practice).

rubrics_metrics.name: "Status life" details
rubrics_metrics.description: Recording everyday details of behavior, possessions, friends, family that indicate a character's social position and identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use material culture and routine behavior as evidence of social status and identity—small, concrete details that illuminate who the subject is and where they fit socially.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth of reporting / attention to minute facts
rubrics_metrics.description: "Depth of reporting and attention to the most minute facts and details that most newspapermen, even the most experienced, have never dreamed of"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters must dig far beyond surface facts; gather many small, specific details that build credibility and texture. This is an essential requirement for effectively rendering scenes and status life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interior monologue from subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Talese: interior monologue from subjects (what they were thinking)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible and supported by reporting, render subjects' unspoken thoughts—reconstruct inner life based on observation, interviews, and corroborating detail, while maintaining factual integrity and attribution practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hours of observation (not just interviews)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hours of observation, not just interviews
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spend extended time physically observing subjects in context to capture behavior, routines, and unguarded moments that interviews alone won't reveal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total immersion in subject's world
rubrics_metrics.description: Total immersion in subject's world
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embed deeply within the subject's environment and social circle to gain access to scenes, details, and authentic voices necessary for scene-by-scene reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject open to extended observation
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject open to extended observation — willing to be followed
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select subjects who permit or tolerate prolonged presence; sustained access is necessary to assemble scenes and dialogue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vivid scene potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Vivid scene potential — places that can be described
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose subjects and contexts that provide visually and sensorially rich settings for scenes; environments that can be vividly rendered strengthen the narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character-driven story
rubrics_metrics.description: Character-driven story — main subject carries narrative
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize stories where a central character's actions, conflicts, and transformations provide narrative drive rather than relying solely on events or expository summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social significance beyond the personal
rubrics_metrics.description: Social significance beyond the personal
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the piece speaks to larger social, cultural, or political themes; the individual's story should illuminate broader issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status detail richness
rubrics_metrics.description: Status detail richness — material culture matters
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect and incorporate many concrete status markers (possessions, habits, acquaintances) to show place in social hierarchy and to make characters tangible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialogue-rich
rubrics_metrics.description: Dialogue-rich — people willing to speak fully
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for subjects and interlocutors who will provide extended, revealing speech; rich dialogue fuels scene construction and character development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Underlying theme
rubrics_metrics.description: Underlying theme — about something larger
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shape the narrative around a discernible theme or argument so the story transcends mere portraiture and situates individual experience within an interpretive frame.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-investment-worthy
rubrics_metrics.description: Time-investment-worthy — pays back hours of reporting
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose projects where the payoff—in insight, narrative interest, and reader value—justifies the extensive reporting and time required by the New Journalism approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity over typicality
rubrics_metrics.description: Specificity over typicality — one specific person reveals universal
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor richly specific characters and scenes that, by their detail, illuminate broader truths rather than using generalized averages or clichéd profiles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process over event
rubrics_metrics.description: Process over event — show how things actually work
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize the unfolding processes, routines, and mechanics behind situations rather than treating isolated events as self-explanatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambiguity tolerance
rubrics_metrics.description: Ambiguity tolerance — don't simplify to fit news template
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept and represent complexity and unresolved aspects of subjects; avoid forcing tidy conclusions when the reporting shows ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original characters (vs. official spokespeople)
rubrics_metrics.description: Original characters — vs. official spokespeople
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek access to primary participants and atypical figures whose perspectives are not mediated through institutional spokespeople; original characters make for more interesting scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcultures as fertile ground
rubrics_metrics.description: Subcultures — rarely covered worlds
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explore insular or marginalized groups and subcultures, which often offer rich, unfamiliar material for scene-driven storytelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scene access
rubrics_metrics.description: Scene access — can the journalist be present?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the reporter can physically attend and observe key moments; without scene access, New Journalism techniques are difficult or impossible to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict factual accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Strict factual accuracy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain rigorous fact-checking and fidelity to verifiable facts even while using literary techniques; factual accuracy is non-negotiable.

rubrics_metrics.name: No composites
rubrics_metrics.description: No composites
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not create composite characters or combine multiple people's actions or words into a single invented source; each scene should be attributable to real individuals and moments.

rubrics_metrics.name: No invented dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: No invented dialogue
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not fabricate conversations; reported dialogue should be based on notes, recordings, or contemporaneous observation and must be accurately attributed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Source attribution
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribute information and lines of reporting appropriately; maintain transparency about sources and how material was obtained to preserve credibility.
